item.title: Fan Favorite Moment From 'Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney' Is An Annual Holiday Season Tradition
item.description: "Almost Christmas" Means It Wasn't Christmas is a line spoken by the character Phoenix Wright in the visual novel, Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney, originally released in mid-October 2001. The catchphrase and scene later became a meme among the video game's fandom and are traditionally posted annually in December, most commonly on December 24th, just before Christmas Day. Variations of the meme include fan art depictions, redraws, exploitables and more.

item.title: Insane 'Charlie Kirk' Movement Goes Viral On TikTok, Reels
item.description: Jerk for Kirk is an ironic social media movement where, on January 6th, 2026, participants are encouraged to masturbate in memory and support of Charlie Kirk, who was killed in September 2025. The movement began gaining momentum on social media in early December 2025, most notably on TikTok, as users posted videos and memes advertising the date and movement under the hashtag "#JerkForKirk."

item.title: Dude In A Crazy Fit Inspires Memes About How To Spot A Filipino
item.description: How Did You Know I'm Filipino is a series of memes, including video edits and AI-generated edits based on an edited image of a Filipino man wearing a flared, baggy jeans, big shoes and a black hoodie, sometimes referred to as an "hourglass fit" for its shape. In December 2025, the image became the subject of memes which suggest that the outfit is a telltale sign that the person is Filipino. item.title: Graph Ranking Well Written Anime Characters Goes Viral, Sparking Discourse And Edits
item.description: Main Characters How Well Written They Are is an exploitable meme format showing a graph of main characters from a variety of anime series, meant to rank how well written they are. The original graph, posted by X / Twitter user @rezeistweeting in late December 2025, ranks One Piece protagonist Monkey D. Luffy as the best written in comparison to characters like Naruto, Goku, Ichigo and more. The post inspired discourse and edits that replace the original characters with other characters.

item.title: Epstein Has Become The Focus Of Countless Viral Fancam Edits In Bizarre Shortform Video Trend
item.description: Jeffrey Epstein Edits refers to fancam-style, often AI-assisted video edits revolving around and often ironically glazing up deceased sex trafficker Jeffrey Epstein. Epstein edits began appearing online as early as January 2024 and saw a boost in virality in December 2025 surrounding the release of the redacted Epstein files. Some of the edits are set to slowed down or otherwise remixed versions of "Boss" by Lil Pump and the "EFN" song.

item.title: On This Day 13 Years Ago, The 'Why Are You Booing Me? I'm Right' Meme Appeared On 'The Eric Andre Show'
item.description: Why Are You Booing Me? I’m Right refers to a reaction image taken from The Eric Andre Show of comedian Hannibal Burress addressing a crowd with the phrase “Why are you booing me? I’m right!” The image began being used with unpopular truths several years after the episode aired.
